## Solution

We seek a holomorphic function $f(z)=u+iv$ with $xu+yv=(x^2+y^2)e^x\cos y$.

**Key identity.** For $z=x+iy$ and $f=u+iv$,
$$\bar z\, f(z)=(x-iy)(u+iv)=\underbrace{(xu+yv)}_{\Re(\bar z f)}+i(xv-yu).$$
Hence the condition is exactly
$$\Re\!\big(\bar z\, f(z)\big)=(x^2+y^2)e^x\cos y.$$

**Constructing a solution.** Since $|z|^2=x^2+y^2$ and $\Re(e^z)=e^x\cos y$,
$$(x^2+y^2)e^x\cos y=|z|^2\Re(e^z)=\Re\!\big(|z|^2 e^z\big)=\Re\!\big(\bar z\,(z e^z)\big).$$
Thus $f(z)=z e^z$ is a solution. Explicitly, $z e^z=(x+iy)e^x(\cos y+i\sin y)$, so
$$u=e^x(x\cos y-y\sin y),\qquad v=e^x(x\sin y+y\cos y),$$
and
$$xu+yv=e^x\big[x^2\cos y-xy\sin y+xy\sin y+y^2\cos y\big]=e^x(x^2+y^2)\cos y.\;\checkmark$$

**Determining all solutions.** Suppose $h$ is holomorphic and also satisfies $\Re(\bar z\,h)=0$; then $f=ze^z+h$ is the general solution. Expand $h(z)=\sum_{n\ge 0}c_n z^n$ with $c_n=\alpha_n+i\beta_n$. On $|z|=r$ ($z=re^{i\theta}$),
$$\Re(\bar z\,h)=\sum_{n\ge 0}r^{n+1}\Re\!\big(c_n e^{i(n-1)\theta}\big)=0\quad\text{for all }\theta,r.$$
Grouping by Fourier frequency:
- **Frequency $0$** (only $n=1$): $\alpha_1 r^2=0\Rightarrow \alpha_1=0$.
- **Frequency $k\ge 2$** (only $n=k+1$): $\alpha_{k+1}\cos k\theta-\beta_{k+1}\sin k\theta=0\Rightarrow c_{k+1}=0$, so $c_n=0$ for $n\ge 3$.
- **Frequency $1$** (from $n=0$ and $n=2$): $r(\alpha_0\cos\theta+\beta_0\sin\theta)+r^3(\alpha_2\cos\theta-\beta_2\sin\theta)=0$ for all $r$; the $r$- and $r^3$-coefficients vanish separately, giving $c_0=0$ and $c_2=0$.

Thus $h(z)=i\beta_1 z=iCz$ for an arbitrary real constant $C$, and one checks $\Re(\bar z\cdot iCz)=\Re(iC|z|^2)=0$.

**Conclusion.** The holomorphic functions satisfying the condition are
$$\boxed{\,f(z)=z e^z+iCz,\qquad C\in\mathbb{R}\,}$$
with the principal (and simplest) member $f(z)=z e^z$.
